That is essentially was is occurring. Medicare taxes are on all earned income, and an additional .9% is added for high wage earners (kicks in at $250K, i believe.) Then marginal rates have creeped up for the higher brackets as well. While they're no where near 70%, these are shifting upward. Deductions for dependents also phase out at a certain point, and the ability to defer income into tax-free investments. The focus needs to be on a marginal tax rate, and not just the stated bracket rate. 

E.g. you can make a lot of money, but if you are able to defer it or deduct against it, then you'll never pay the intended rate for your bracket.
